tasks.short: Check purchase order claims and contracts against purchasing policy, then resolve exceptions.

steps.what: Retrieve purchase order claims, contracts and applicable purchasing policy.
Read contract clauses and identify terms relevant to the claim.

loop.input: Contract text, claim details and a fixed contract-field schema.
loop.output: Proposed contract fields with clause quotations and page references.
loop.check: Check quotations against the document, validate types and flag conflicting clauses; a person confirms relevant fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; missing or conflicting terms go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant terms appear in varied prose and amendments rather than consistent fields.

steps.what: Compare claim amounts and contract terms against the policy checklist.
Decide whether exceptions require correction, legal advice or an authorised waiver.
Record the decision and route correction requests to the responsible team.

tasks.design: An integration assembles claims from the {PROCUREMENT} and contracts from the {CLM}; a bounded extraction loop proposes cited contract fields. Deterministic rules compare confirmed fields with versioned policy, and the {WORKFLOW} routes exceptions for a decision before recording results in the {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contract amendments were difficult to turn into reliable fields, and policy checks crossed separate records.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can propose cited fields, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building connectors and rule checks.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting amendments, disputed claims and ambiguous policy remain expensive to resolve.
tasks.human_edge: Judge commercial context and decide when an exception needs legal advice or higher approval.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time finding clauses and more time resolving exceptions early. Waiver and spending authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Document version control, clause references and exception routing
Policy checks and how contract amendments affect orders

evidence.claim: Structured policy checks can use deterministic rules; contract prose may require reviewed extraction.
Transporeon Freight Audit checks carrier invoices against agreed rates; this supports the narrower rate-checking pattern.

assumptions: Claims reference identifiable purchase orders and contract versions.
A spreadsheet checklist bridges contract review and purchasing records today.
Policy includes explicit thresholds alongside judgement-based exceptions.
Build ranges cover one claim type and one policy set.
Confidential documents stay within approved access and retention controls.
unknowns: Which claim types and contract amendments are most common?
Are policy thresholds machine-readable and versioned?
Who may approve each waiver value and category?
Which interfaces and document permissions are available?
Does implementation require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: How often does extraction miss a relevant amendment in representative review files?
Which checks produce reliable findings without contract interpretation?
new_work: Confirm extracted clauses and resolve conflicting document versions.
Maintain policy rules and their effective dates.
Investigate missing links between claims, orders and contracts.
Sample completed reviews and maintain integration logs.

tasks.short: Review bid specifications, approve tender release and evaluate proposed awards.

steps.what: Collect the draft specification, business need, budget and proposed evaluation criteria.
Check requirements for completeness, contradictions and potentially restrictive wording.

loop.input: Draft specification, required sections and approved review guidance.
loop.output: Potential contradictions, omissions and restrictive clauses with source references.
loop.check: Validate section checks deterministically; the manager confirms each substantive finding against the specification.
loop.stop: One review and one repair attempt per specification; unresolved findings remain open for human review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Semantic contradictions and restrictive wording cannot all be detected with field checks.

steps.what: Agree necessary requirements, acceptable alternatives and evaluation trade-offs with the requester.
Approve the specification and criteria for tender release.
Issue the approved tender package to the selected suppliers.
Compare received bids with the approved specification and evaluation criteria.

loop.input: Supplier bids and the approved bid-comparison schema.
loop.output: Cited prices, delivery terms, exclusions and claimed requirement coverage.
loop.check: Recalculate totals in code; verify citations and missing fields; a buyer confirms technical interpretation and recommendation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per bid; unclear compliance stays unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier proposals use varied formats and prose exclusions; arithmetic and scoring remain deterministic.

steps.what: Approve the award recommendation or request further evaluation.

tasks.design: The {PROCUREMENT} collects a versioned tender package, while bounded loops flag specification issues and extract bid facts into a comparison. Deterministic checks calculate totals and apply approved criteria; people agree requirements and approve release and award. The {PARTNER_PORTAL} issues only the frozen package and supplier list authorised at release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications and bids arrived as varied documents, and approval trails did not consistently preserve the exact reviewed version.
tasks.enabler_now: Cited document review and extraction can support existing tender workflows, with small custom comparison tools built faster.
tasks.still_hard: Technical equivalence, biased requirements and value-versus-risk trade-offs require domain knowledge.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge unnecessary requirements and defend a commercially sound, fair award decision.

ambition.what: Early specification review for first-time technical requesters

tasks.altitude: The manager can review requirements earlier and spend more time on technical and commercial trade-offs. Tender and award authority remain within the existing approval matrix.

reach.learn: Requirement traceability, total-cost calculations and handling bid exclusions

reach.task: Compare product alternatives before a sourcing decision
reach.learn: Specification equivalence and demand-sensitive evaluation criteria

evidence.claim: Versioned approvals, arithmetic checks and bid-comparison templates can be implemented deterministically.
Document models can propose cited specification findings and bid fields, but technical equivalence requires review.

assumptions: This is ordinary company purchasing; any special tender obligations must be identified separately.
Technical requesters remain responsible for validating technical requirements.
Tender approval covers the exact package and recipient list before external release.
The comparison spreadsheet is a common bridge between supplier documents and approval records.
Build ranges cover one tender category and one comparison schema.
unknowns: Which tender obligations apply to this organisation?
Who approves specifications, supplier lists and awards at each value?
Does the current tender workflow preserve approved versions?
Which categories require specialist technical evaluation?
What supplier confidentiality and document-access restrictions apply?
research_questions: Which specification findings do technical reviewers consider useful?
How accurately can bid exclusions be mapped to approved requirements?
new_work: Review proposed specification findings and extracted bid facts.
Maintain category-specific templates and evaluation criteria.
Check that issued packages match approved versions.

tasks.short: Maintain purchasing access, catalogues, approval routes and system reliability.

steps.what: Review purchasing support requests and prioritise access, catalogue and workflow issues.
Inspect user permissions, catalogue records, approval routes and failed transactions.
Agree the business impact and authorise permission or approval-route changes.
Configure the authorised change in a test environment and run transaction checks.
Approve the tested configuration for production release.
Apply the approved configuration, document the change and notify affected users.
Review transaction failures, stale access and recurring purchasing support problems.

tasks.design: Configure structured requests and change approvals in the {HELPDESK}, and use deterministic checks to surface permission conflicts and failed transactions from the {PROCUREMENT} and {ERP}. Approved configuration packages pass through test and release controls, with automatic records and notices. An aggregate {BI} dashboard shows service problems without scoring individual employees.
tasks.previous_blocker: Configuration changes relied on administrator knowledge, scattered logs and repeated manual checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration tools handle much of the work; AI-assisted coding makes log connectors and repeatable checks cheaper.
tasks.still_hard: Cross-system permissions, segregation of duties and configuration dependencies need careful testing. GDPR applies to staff data; consultation requirements depend on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Balance ease of purchasing with financial control and judge the impact of changes on teams.

ambition.what: Time-limited purchasing access for temporary project buyers

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time on service improvements and control design, with fewer routine support interruptions. Access and release decisions remain within the existing delegated authority.

reach.task: Resolve routine catalogue and access requests
reach.learn: Structured diagnosis, permission boundaries and escalation

reach.task: Validate approval routes for purchasing scenarios
reach.learn: Transaction testing and segregation of duties

evidence.claim: Structured service requests, permission checks and configuration approvals usually need configuration and deterministic checks.
Staff-data access and workflow changes may require consultation under national rules.

assumptions: A purchasing system administrator supports the manager, possibly within the IT team.
Structured request categories cover routine support; unusual requests are escalated.
A test environment and supported configuration promotion are available.
Release automation applies only the exact approved configuration.
Build ranges cover routine changes and aggregate service reporting, without employee performance scoring.
unknowns: Which configuration changes can be promoted through supported interfaces?
Who owns access, approval-route and production-release decisions?
Are test environments and representative transaction cases available?
Which national consultation rules and employee agreements apply?
How long do access approval and any required consultation take?
research_questions: Which recurring failures can be detected from structured logs?
Can configuration promotion preserve approval evidence and support rollback?
new_work: Maintain request categories and diagnostic checks.
Review permission conflicts and unfamiliar failures.
Update test cases when purchasing rules change.
Maintain release records, rollback packages and access reviews.

tasks.short: Turn supply and equipment requests into approved requisitions and purchase orders.

steps.what: Check incoming purchase requests for required details and attachments.
Clarify missing requirements, quantities and delivery needs with the requester.
Check the selected catalogue item or quote against agreed supplier terms.

loop.input: Non-catalogue quote, requested items and confirmed contract fields.
loop.output: Proposed item, price, currency, quantity and delivery fields with quote references.
loop.check: Validate types, recalculate totals and compare contract terms; a buyer confirms proposed fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per quote; discrepancies go to a buyer. Catalogue orders bypass the loop.
loop.why_not_simpler: Non-catalogue quotes contain varied tables and prose; structured catalogue orders need only deterministic checks.

steps.what: Create the requisition with supplier, cost centre, items and supporting documents.
Approve the requisition's business need, budget and order terms.
Convert the approved requisition into a purchase order and check copied details.
Send the purchase order to the supplier and record dispatch.

tasks.design: Configure required request fields, catalogue checks, approval routing and order conversion in the {PROCUREMENT}, using budget and supplier records from the {ERP}. A bounded loop proposes fields only for unstructured quotes; buyers handle ambiguity and budget owners approve commitments. Orders dispatch through the {EMAIL} only when their supplier, items, quantities and commercial terms match the approved requisition.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incomplete requests, document quotes and repeated entry prevented reliable order conversion, despite existing purchasing features.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing purchasing configuration covers the main flow, and reviewed quote extraction handles a limited document gap.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear equipment requirements, changed quotes, emergency purchases and supplier-data errors remain exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the real need and challenge unnecessary or unsuitable purchases before committing money.

ambition.what: Guided equipment ordering for occasional departmental requesters

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time supervising order entry and more time resolving unusual needs and improving purchasing service. Spending limits and budget-owner decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Manage order dispatch failures and incomplete supplier records
reach.learn: Exception queues, supplier-data validation and approval traceability

evidence.claim: Required fields, catalogue ordering, approval routing and requisition conversion are standard purchasing workflow patterns.
Unstructured quotes can use bounded extraction, while calculations and approval matching remain deterministic.

assumptions: Most requests already enter a purchasing screen; email mainly handles clarification and supplier dispatch.
This screen-based flow differs from the document-heavy prior because requisitions and orders are structured records.
Confirmed contract fields are reused from contract review rather than extracted again.
Approval covers the exact commitment subsequently sent to the supplier.
Build ranges cover one request flow and one supplier-dispatch channel.
Any additional requester effort from required fields is included when measuring net savings.
unknowns: What share of requests use catalogues, quotes or informal messages?
Can current configuration convert and dispatch approved orders?
Which changes invalidate requisition approval?
Are supplier records and budget balances reliable?
Who approves emergency purchases and exceptions?
Do workflow changes require consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which missing request fields cause the most clarification work?
Does configured ordering reduce total handling time across requesters, buyers and approvers?
new_work: Review extracted quote fields and contract discrepancies.
Handle incomplete requests and unusual requirements.
Maintain catalogue records, approval routes and request guidance.
Resolve dispatch failures and prevent duplicate orders.

role.altitude: The purchasing manager spends more of the week on specification quality, supplier risk, exceptions and purchasing service. Existing financial authority stays unchanged; wider decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Help purchasing agents make evidence-backed sourcing recommendations.
Help procurement clerks manage reliable records and exception queues.
Help wholesale and retail buyers compare commercially relevant product alternatives.
skills_to_grow: Translate purchasing policy into testable checks.
Review cited document extraction and recognise uncertainty.
Design approval boundaries and preserve decision evidence.
Measure total handling time across all participating roles.
Evaluate technical equivalence and commercial trade-offs.
role.ambitious_version: Offer early specification advice and guided ordering to occasional requesters, while using frequent exception reviews to identify avoidable purchasing problems.
